title: Windows paths
description:
Write the path handling of lesson 5.01 (on `std::string`, with `\` as the separator; `/` is accepted as one too):

```cpp
std::string pathRoot(const std::string& path);         // "C:\", "C:", "\", "\\server\share\" or ""
bool isAbsolute(const std::string& path);              // "C:\..." or "\\server\share..."
std::string normalize(const std::string& path);
std::string join(const std::string& base, const std::string& more);
std::string withLongPrefix(const std::string& path);
```

- **pathRoot**: `C:\x` → `C:\` (drive absolute), `C:x` → `C:` (drive relative), `\x` → `\` (root relative), `\\server\share\x` → `\\server\share\`, a relative path → `""`. Drive letters may be either case; returned roots use `\`.
- **normalize**: turn `/` into `\`, collapse repeated separators (except the two at the start of a UNC root), remove `.` parts, and let `..` remove the previous part; a `..` that would go above the root is dropped when there is a root, and kept for a relative path (`..\..\x` stays). A trailing separator is removed, except for the root itself. An empty result of a relative path is `"."`.
- **join**: if `more` has any root (`pathRoot(more)` is not empty), it replaces `base`... except a root-relative `more` (`\x`) keeps `base`'s drive (`C:\a` + `\x` = `C:\x`). Otherwise `base + "\" + more`. The result is normalized.
- **withLongPrefix**: paths of 260 characters or more get `\\?\` (`\\?\C:\...`), and UNC paths get `\\?\UNC\server\share\...`; shorter paths and relative paths are returned unchanged. Normalize first.
hints: Split the work in two: find the root first (and how many characters it uses), then treat the rest as a list of parts separated by `\` or `/`, and finally join the root and parts back together.
